clue.text: Twin found gold

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it in a mould
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Someone, or a twin, strikes it rich by finding gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Castor and Pollux are the Heavenly Twins of Greek myth, the Gemini. 'Found' looks like the past of 'find' but is the foundry verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In mythology Castor was one of the Dioscuri, twin brother of Pollux.

clue.text: Tom's high-rise accommodation in tents on a river

parts.note: a camp is lodging under canvas
the Nile is the river of Egypt

explanation.surface: A tom cat's high-rise flat is a tent pitched by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a cat or a man, but Great Tom is a famous bell, so its high-rise is a bell tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-standing bell tower houses a great bell such as Great Tom.

clue.text: Like this clue describing eg sugar in tea?

explanation.surface: A self-referring clue compares itself with sugar stirred into tea.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is able to be solved, like any fair clue; the other is able to dissolve.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue that can be worked out can be solved, and sugar dissolves in hot liquid.

clue.text: Eclipse — how he used to dominate the field

definitions.text: how he used to dominate the field

explanation.surface: A champion's eclipse of rivals is how he once dominated.
explanation.walkthrough: Eclipse was the unbeaten 18th-century racehorse ('Eclipse first, the rest nowhere'), so 'he' is that horse and the field is the other runners.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse is to put in the shade, which is how the great horse treated every rival.

clue.text: Beetle's penalty for too much indulgence?

explanation.surface: A beetle is being punished for overeating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beetle' is a verb here: beetling brows project, so to beetle is to jut out above something. The second sense is the morning after drinking too much.
explanation.definitionFit: To beetle is to project outward above, and the after-effect of heavy drinking is the morning-after headache of the same name.

clue.text: Dramatic title role -a customer for Burke and Hare

definitions.text: a customer for Burke and Hare

explanation.surface: An actor's starring part is a client of the Edinburgh body-snatchers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Anatomist is James Bridie's play about Dr Robert Knox, who bought corpses from the Edinburgh murderers Burke and Hare for dissection.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Knox, a dissecting surgeon, both names Bridie's play and bought bodies from the murderers.

clue.text: Trick put up to get round the credit-transfer system

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word is written upwards

parts.note: to rig is to fix or trick
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A trick is set up to dodge the bank's credit-transfer system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns RIG into GIR. A giro is the British bank and Post Office credit-transfer system.
explanation.definitionFit: A banking scheme transferring money directly between accounts goes by this name in Britain and Europe.

clue.text: Supply with provisions cut in pieces in a small bottle

indicators.note: the second in places the rearranged letters within the bottle

parts.note: a vial is a small glass bottle

indicators.note: cut in pieces, its letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Food supplies are chopped up and stored in a little bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in pieces' makes CTU from CUT, and the second 'in' puts it inside VIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Victuals are food, so as a verb it means to stock with food supplies.

clue.text: Pine extract engineer found over the' wilderness

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
the Wilderness of Sin is where the Israelites wandered in Exodus

explanation.surface: An engineer finds pine sap out in the wilds.
explanation.walkthrough: The wilderness is the biblical Wilderness of Sin, crossed by the Israelites after the Red Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The sticky substance exuded by pine trees is a tree gum.

clue.text: Deal arranged by 1 ac's mother

indicators.note: arranged letters are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A bargain is struck by someone's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 across is CASTOR; in myth his mother was the queen seduced by Zeus as a swan.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Spartan queen bore the Dioscuri twins after Zeus came to her as a swan.

clue.text: Dramatist is one who wrote Utopia without fabrication

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the author's name goes around the lie

parts.note: Sir Thomas More wrote Utopia (1516)
a fabrication is a lie

explanation.surface: A playwright is said to be the author of Utopia, but without invention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as 'lacking' but here means outside, so MORE wraps LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French comic playwright of Tartuffe is a dramatist.

clue.text: Wild animal once of the bovine or such a variety

definitions.text: Wild animal once of the bovine

indicators.note: a variety of the letters means they are rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: An extinct wild beast belonging to the cattle family, or some such type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' turns OR SUCH A into the wild ox's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The extinct wild ox of Europe, ancestor of domestic cattle, was a bovine beast of long ago.

clue.text: As a diplomat he appears in capital form

definitions.text: As a diplomat he appears in capital form

parts.words: As a diplomat he appears in capital form
parts.note: a senior envoy is posted in a foreign capital, and appears there in full formal dress or style

explanation.surface: A diplomat turns up in the capital in proper form.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest-ranking envoy is resident in a foreign capital and is addressed formally as His Excellency.

clue.text: Go for a short walk

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a brief stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is a noun: your go is your turn in a game. 'Go for' looks like a verb phrase, but 'for' only links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A go in a game is one's chance to play, and a brief stroll is taking a few steps around.

clue.text: On which Alice won her promotion

definitions.text: On which Alice won her promotion

parts.words: On which Alice won her promotion
parts.note: in Through the Looking-Glass Alice is a pawn who crosses the board and becomes a queen

explanation.surface: The place where Alice earned her promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promotion' sounds like a job, but it is a pawn reaching the last rank and becoming a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's sequel sets Alice's journey on a giant game board of squares.

clue.text: Keep saying it was, classically, the origin of earth

parts.note: taken as written
erat is Latin for 'was', the classical language

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pedant goes on repeating what the earth's origin was in classical times.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat something over and over is to say it again and again.

clue.text: Former adaptation of Welsh rite

indicators.note: an adaptation reshapes material, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A Welsh ceremony is an altered version of an older one.
explanation.definitionFit: An erstwhile friend is one who was so in the past, a one-time friend.

clue.text: Was this smoker more healthy in the first place?

indicators.note: the first place tells us the word in stands at the front

parts.note: taken as written
hale means healthy, so haler is more healthy

explanation.surface: Was this smoker in better health to begin with?
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the first place' reads as 'originally' but says IN comes first, before HALER.
explanation.definitionFit: One who draws smoke into the lungs breathes it in deeply, as opposed to a puffer.

clue.text: Comply with request to forward study outfit

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
a dress is an outfit

explanation.surface: A clothes shop sends on a study outfit as asked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comply with request to forward' is the post office instruction on a letter: put a new address on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail sent on to a new location has a fresh address written on it.

clue.text: To prepare for execution may so occupy a law clerk's attention

explanation.surface: A law clerk's attention is taken up by drafting deeds for signing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Execution' is the signing of a legal deed, not a hanging: to engross a deed is to write out its final fair copy ready for signature.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer's fair copy of a deed is written out ready for signing, and to absorb someone's attention wholly is to hold it.

clue.text: Chemical warfare ploy said to be affecting the inner man

indicators.note: said to be marks a sound-alike

parts.note: a gas trick, a ruse using poison gas

explanation.surface: A poison-gas ploy upsets the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The inner man' is an old phrase for the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the stomach, which jocularly is the inner man.

clue.text: Hardy lass has time for a bit of mosaic work

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: One of Thomas Hardy's heroines takes time out to do some mosaic.
explanation.definitionFit: A small square tile of stone or glass is one piece of a mosaic.

clue.text: In mid-week send for the recluse

indicators.note: In places the sending word inside the two middle letters
mid gives the central letters of the word week

parts.note: to remit is to send money

explanation.surface: Halfway through the week someone calls for the hermit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-' gives EE from 'week', and 'In' puts REMIT between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit living alone for religious reasons is an old word for a solitary.

clue.text: Is it hard for the creditor to get?

definitions.text: Is it hard for the creditor to get?

parts.words: Is it hard for the creditor to get?
parts.note: hard here is the money sense, as in coins and notes, which a lender may find difficult to recover

explanation.surface: A lender wonders whether repayment will be difficult to obtain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard' suggests difficult, but hard money is coins and notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready money in coins and notes is what a lender wants back.

clue.text: Milton's work, sounds like "The Shaggy Dogs' Plea"

indicators.note: sounds like says the words are heard, not spelt

parts.note: shaggy dogs would beg their owners 'comb us'

explanation.surface: A Milton title is likened to a request from scruffy dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: Comus is Milton's masque of 1634; said aloud it is 'comb us', with a silent B.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's masque performed at Ludlow Castle is one of his poetic works.

clue.text: Sugar-loaf unobtainable at the confectioner's

parts.note: read as a sugary loaf, it ought to be in a sweetshop, but the name belongs to offal sold by butchers

explanation.surface: A sweetshop has run out of sugar-loaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as sugar plus loaf the name suggests a cake; in fact it is the thymus or pancreas of a calf or lamb, cooked as offal.
explanation.definitionFit: The thymus gland of a calf, eaten as a delicacy, carries a name meaning sugary loaf yet is meat.

clue.text: Remark especially — ie call out

indicators.note: call out means pronounce these letters as one word

parts.note: ESP is a standard abbreviation for especially; taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone makes a comment, notably that is, shouting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remark' is the verb meaning notice. ESP and IE said together sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To remark something in the old sense is to notice or catch sight of it.

clue.text: Game with northern diving bird

parts.note: loo is an old card game

explanation.surface: A game played with a northern diving bird.
explanation.walkthrough: In North America the loon is the bird the British call a diver.
explanation.definitionFit: The great northern diver, called a loon in America, plunges underwater for fish.

clue.text: His invention was instrumental in Crippen's capture

definitions.text: His invention was instrumental in Crippen's capture

parts.words: His invention was instrumental in Crippen's capture
parts.note: Dr Crippen, the 1910 murderer fleeing to Canada by ship, was caught after the captain sent a wireless telegraph message

explanation.surface: An inventor's device helped to catch the murderer Crippen.
explanation.walkthrough: Crippen's arrest in 1910 was the first time a criminal was caught with the help of wireless telegraphy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian pioneer of radio telegraphy built the apparatus that let a ship's captain report the fugitive.

clue.text: Sweet little couple having a row

parts.note: pr is the short form of pair, a couple
a row is a line

explanation.surface: A sweet young pair are having an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel to fit the couple, but it is a straight line.
explanation.definitionFit: A confection of nuts in caramelised sugar is a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Supporter or representative of modern monarchy

explanation.surface: A royalist backs the present monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: At the time of printing the monarch was Elizabeth II, so a second ER (Elizabeth Regina) represents the modern monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: One who backs a motion supports the proposer, and Elizabeth the Second's royal cipher was ER.

clue.text: Dreads squirming poison- ous creatures

indicators.note: squirming letters twist about, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fears writhing venomous snakes.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder is Britain's only venomous snake, so these are poisonous creatures.
